newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Bonos closed sharply higher on Tuesday after long bond futures hit a new record high, tracking the positive mood of other major bonds.
The "Spanish bond market was really strong during all the day. It's just ending a little bit softer," said Emilio Sainz, dealer at Natwest in Madrid.
The Bank of Spain's decision to mantain its key money market rate, as expected, left the market with even greater hopes it could cut rates at its next repo on December 13.
"I'm convinced they'll cut that day by 25 basis points," said Jose Ramon Nunez at Benito y Monjardin in Madrid.
Dealers described Treasury auctions this morning as a success. On the new 10-year bond, with a lower 7.35-percent coupon, the yield declined to 6.915 percent from 7.804 percent a month ago.
At the close, the 10-year benchmark traded at 112.91 from 112.27 on Monday and yielded 6.87 percent.
"Prices went up so fast that the auction came out with a high yield in comparison with the secondary market," said Nunez.
But the three-year bond, allotted at 5.905 percent and a price of 100.35, versus 6.829 percent and 97.10, respectively, traded lower around 100.23 at the end of the day.
"We saw a big trader selling in the three-year segment," explained Avelino Gonzalez, dealer at Deutsche Bank in Madrid.
On Wednesday, Treasury will tender five- and 15-year bonds.
"I do not expect huge demand because this part of the yield curve is really expensive," Gonzalez said.
The 7.90-percent five-year bond traded at 105.65 from Monday's 105.13 and yielded 6.21 percent. A month ago, these were allotted at 102.10 with a 6.907-percent yield.
But others expected the five-year auction to be well bid.
"I expect very good demand in this segment," said Sainz, who saw further yield curve flattening.
"People will buy these maturities in anticipation of a possible rate cut on December 13," said Nunez.
German bunds led gains, though they were partly erased later in the day after Bundesbank rate remarks.
The Bundesbank stressed no rate change was expected in the short term.
The 10-year spread between bonos and Bunds ended the day at an all-time low of 125 basis points versus around 131 on Monday.
